paper_metadata.title: Fecocrnimo high-entropy alloys prepared by powder metallurgy processing for diamond tool applications

evidence.quote: Here, we report the formation of FeCoCrNiMo HEAs by powder metallurgy processing, starting from a gas-atomised powder followed by mechanical milling and consolidation by spark plasma sintering.

To compare the wear behaviour of our samples with that of the metal-matrix of commercial diamond tools, a reference specimen with code HFXP-58 (a metal-matrix of the diamond tool that has the best performance available in the Chinese market currently) was tested under the same conditions.
The powder with a nominal composition Fe 24.1Co24.1-Cr24.1Ni24.1Mo3.6 (all compositions are in atomic per cent (at.-%) throughout the article) was prepared by gas atomisation.

Next, the powder with a particle size under 200 mesh was mechanically milled using conventional planetary milling equipment. The weight ratio between the powder and the stainless-steel balls was 1:10 and ethanol was added as the milling medium. The milling time was 20 h and the milling speed was 300 rev min

Analysis of the XRD patterns in Figure 2 shows that both gas-atomised and milled powders have the same crystallographic structure where all the reflections can be indexed to a pure FCC crystal structure.
All the sintered specimens show the pure FCC structure similar to the gas-atomised and milled powders, and no reflections from other phases, such as intermetallic brittle phases, are detected.
Figure 1 (b) shows that the powder has a cellular or dendrite-cellular structure on the surface of the particles, and this structure depends on the particle size.

attributes.morphology: spherical or near-spherical with satellite structure

evidence.quote: The gas-atomised powder has a spherical or near-spherical morphology with some satellite structure, as shown in Figure 1(a).
all the microstructures exhibit a uniform contrast except for the positions of remnant pores, which were not closed during SPS process.
The grain size of the sample sintered at 30 MPa and 1000°C is around 300 nm [11] and increases to around 500 nm in the sample sintered at 1100°C with the same pressure.
The grain size of the sample sintered at 30 MPa and 1000°C is around 300 nm [11] and increases to around 500 nm in the sample sintered at 1100°C with the same pressure.
For a sintering temperature of 1100°C, although the density increases with pressure, the grain size of the HEAs decreases with pressure. It increases to about 700 nm when sintering at 40 MPa.
The highest density of about 8.19 g/cm3, which is very close to the theoretical density of 8.286 g/cm3, can be obtained by sintering at 1100°C under 40 MPa.
